quotes.speaker: Kevin Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Porter Jr. on the Milwaukee Bucks' offensive identity
quotes.excerpt: I think it's pretty simple, you know, attack space, take what the defense gives us
quotes.quote: I think it's pretty simple, you know, attack space, take what the defense gives us and also just be basketball players. And I think we have an identity when we drive, depending on where the drive comes from, baseline or if it's slot or if it's driving middle. As a team we know what to do, and I think that's great. Especially as a PG, I love the blind pass, so guys just being in the spot, you know, you just throw it in. We hope you trust the guys there and that's what we've been drilling, so it's been moving. It's been good.
quotes.social_post: Kevin Porter Jr. on the Bucks offensive identity: It is about attacking space, taking what the defense gives, and just being basketball players. He says the team is drilling trust and spacing to make the system work.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Porter Jr. on his role as a cutter
quotes.excerpt: I feel like a really good cutter and I know how to space out
quotes.quote: If it's not perfect, I feel like a really good cutter and I know how to space out. So I think it's an easy thing to adjust to. I'm really not adjusting, like I said, I think it's something that just is a part of our offense identity, like I said before, and we just got to get our reps at it.
quotes.social_post: Kevin Porter Jr. says he is comfortable adjusting to his role as a cutter in the Bucks offense, noting that it is a core part of their identity that the team is currently repping.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Porter Jr. on the development of Nate and Braden
quotes.excerpt: Nate has been improving, kind of getting out his shell
quotes.quote: Unfortunately what happened to Nate, of course, Nate's from day one, you know, Nate has been improving, kind of getting out his shell. He's already kind of quiet, so spending some time with him, he's been getting better. And everyone knows Braden, like Braden's ahead of his time, ahead of his age. He's a sponge, he asks a lot of questions and I think he's been the game and the pace has been getting to him, he's been feeling it, so that's good.
quotes.social_post: Kevin Porter Jr. praises rookie Braden for being ahead of his age. He says the young guard is a sponge who asks a lot of questions and is already feeling the pace of the NBA game.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Porter Jr. on mentoring Braden
quotes.excerpt: I want him to come in here and stay aggressive, not really take a backseat to anything
quotes.quote: At the end of the day, everyone comes from being that guy usually. And I'm trying to really, I want him to come in here and stay aggressive, not really take a backseat to anything. I try to have him on ball most of practice so I can talk him through some things. And he's been great at receiving and, you know, like I say, he asks a lot of questions and he's been improving and getting better nine day every day. So sky's the limit for for Braden.
quotes.social_post: Kevin Porter Jr. is pushing rookie Braden to stay aggressive in practice. He says he tries to guard him personally during drills to help him learn and improve every day.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Porter Jr. on his health and off-season
quotes.excerpt: I feel like I'm the strongest I've been
quotes.quote: I feel like I'm the strongest I've been. I had a unique off-season, you know, I've never been injured like that, never had surgeries in my life. So it was the first time for me, and I found a appreciation of the game a little deeper. My purpose has grown, and I think this is going to be the best year for me individually.
quotes.social_post: Kevin Porter Jr. says he feels the strongest he has ever been. After dealing with his first career injuries and surgeries, he says his purpose has grown and he expects this to be his best year individually.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Porter Jr. on the leadership of Pat Connaughton
quotes.excerpt: I think he's one of the guys each and every practice that sets the tone
quotes.quote: Pat Connaughton, man, Pat Connaughton, I think he's one of the guys each and every practice that sets the tone. He can, it's vocally, energy, physically, whatever it is. I love Pat Connaughton individually. I tell him to guard me because he don't make it easy for me. You know, he hack, he talk, he try to get in my head and he's like that with everyone. So we love Pat Connaughton, we love his energy and like I said, he sets the tone and you know, guys like that is why, you know, there's champions.
quotes.social_post: Kevin Porter Jr. credits Pat Connaughton for setting the tone at every Bucks practice. He says Connaughton brings energy and physicality that forces everyone to be better.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Porter Jr. on the importance of detail and consistency
quotes.excerpt: We have the blueprint as far as consistency, I think that's the only thing we really need
quotes.quote: I think, you know, we have the blueprint as far as consistency, I think that's the only thing we really need to hone on to. It's detail to being physical and pressure in the ball and intentionally cutting and intentionally spacing. I think that's the the small detail that you do that at a consistent basis, you're going to be one of those teams. And I think that's what Coach Taylor is just trying to do for us every day is make sure that's the main thing.
quotes.social_post: Kevin Porter Jr. believes the Bucks have the blueprint for success but need to hone in on consistency. He says Coach Taylor is emphasizing small details like physical pressure and intentional spacing.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Porter Jr. on team chemistry and off-court bonding
quotes.excerpt: When you guys have a great group of guys that you can come to work
quotes.quote: Like I said, it's a team. This this this this league has a lot outside of basketball. So when you guys have a great group of guys that you can come to work and be happy and ready to work with, it changes a lot of things outside of these four lines. And I think this year we've been doing a good job of just spending time together, kind of being uncomfortable and being comfortable being uncomfortable with each other. But yeah, the the main thing is spending time together and just being boys off the court.
quotes.social_post: Kevin Porter Jr. highlights the importance of team chemistry, noting that the Bucks have been spending significant time together off the court to build trust and comfort with one another.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Porter Jr. on rebounding and transition defense
quotes.excerpt: I've rebounded, so I know how to rebound
quotes.quote: Individually, I've rebounded, so I know how to rebound. But I think we just got to, like I said, everything has requirements and you got to there's a way of doing things. You can't just run in there and rebound, you know, try to we got to tag up, we got to be on the top side, we got to whoever gets the rebound got to deny, deny. There's requirements that we're working on right now with what we want to do. And I think, like I said, this is the time to to square everything up and buckle everything down.
quotes.social_post: Kevin Porter Jr. says the Bucks are working on specific rebounding requirements, including tagging up and denying opponents, to ensure they are disciplined on the glass this season.
